# glob - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/glob/

## Expand description

Support for matching file paths against Unix shell style patterns.

The `glob` and `glob_with` functions allow querying the filesystem for all
files that match a particular pattern (similar to the libc `glob` function).
The methods on the `Pattern` type provide functionality for checking if
individual paths match a particular pattern (similar to the libc `fnmatch`
function).

For consistency across platforms, and for Windows support, this module
is implemented entirely in Rust rather than deferring to the libc
`glob`/`fnmatch` functions.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

To print all jpg files in `/media/` and all of its subdirectories.

```
use glob::glob;
for entry in glob("/media/**/*.jpg").expect("Failed to read glob pattern") {
    match entry {
        Ok(path) => println!("{:?}", path.display()),
        Err(e) => println!("{:?}", e),
    }
}
```
To print all files containing the letter “a”, case insensitive, in a `local`
directory relative to the current working directory. This ignores errors
instead of printing them.

```
use glob::glob_with;
use glob::MatchOptions;
let options = MatchOptions {
    case_sensitive: false,
    require_literal_separator: false,
    require_literal_leading_dot: false,
};
for entry in glob_with("local/*a*", options).unwrap() {
    if let Ok(path) = entry {
        println!("{:?}", path.display())
    }
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Glob](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobError.html)- Error
- A glob iteration error.
- [Match](https://docs.rs/struct.MatchOptions.html)- Options
- Configuration options to modify the behaviour of `Pattern::matches_with(..)`.
- [Paths](https://docs.rs/struct.Paths.html)
- An iterator that yields `Path`s from the filesystem that match a particular pattern.
- [Pattern](https://docs.rs/struct.Pattern.html)
- A compiled Unix shell style pattern.
- [Pattern](https://docs.rs/struct.PatternError.html)- Error
- A pattern parsing error.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [glob](https://docs.rs/fn.glob.html)
- Return an iterator that produces all the `Path`s that match the given pattern using default match options, which may be absolute or relative to the current working directory.
- [glob_](https://docs.rs/fn.glob_with.html)- with
- Return an iterator that produces all the `Path`s that match the given pattern using the specified match options, which may be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Glob](https://docs.rs/type.GlobResult.html)- Result
- An alias for a glob iteration result.

# glob 0.3.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/glob/latest

# glob

Support for matching file paths against Unix shell style patterns.

## Usage

To use `glob`, add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "0.3.2"
```
If you're using Rust 1.30 or earlier, or edition 2015, add this to your crate root:

```
extern crate glob;
```
## Examples

Print all jpg files in /media/ and all of its subdirectories.

```
use glob;
for entry in glob.expect
```

# doc_comment - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/doc-comment/^0.3/

## Expand description

The point of this (small) crate is to allow you to add doc comments from macros or
to test external markdown files’ code blocks through `rustdoc`.

Starting in Rust 1.54, this crate becomes useless as you can do the same thing
with the `doc` attribute:

[§](https://docs.rs#including-files-for-testing)Including file(s) for testing

Let’s assume you want to test code examples in your `README.md` file which
looks like this:

```
# A crate
Here is a code example:
```rust
let x = 2;
assert!(x != 0);
```
```
You can use the `doc_comment!` macro to test it like this:

```
#[macro_use]
extern crate doc_comment;
// When running `cargo test`, rustdoc will check this file as well.
doc_comment!(include_str!("../README.md"));
```
Please note that can also use the `doctest!` macro to have a shorter way to test an outer
file:

```
#[macro_use]
extern crate doc_comment;
doctest!("../README.md");
```
Please also note that you can use `#[cfg(doctest)]`:

```
#[cfg(doctest)]
doctest!("../README.md");
```
In this case, the examples in the `README.md` file will only be run on `cargo test`. You
can find more information about `#[cfg(doctest)]` in [this blogpost](https://blog.guillaume-gomez.fr/articles/2020-03-07+cfg%28doctest%29+is+stable+and+you+should+use+it).

[§](https://docs.rs#generic-documentation)Generic documentation

Now let’s imagine you want to write documentation once for multiple types but still having examples specific to each type:

```
// The macro which generates types
macro_rules! gen_types {
    ($tyname:ident) => {
        /// This is a wonderful generated struct!
        ///
        /// You can use it as follow:
        ///
        /// ```
        /// let x = FirstOne {
        ///     field1: 0,
        ///     field2: 0,
        ///     field3: 0,
        ///     field4: 0,
        /// };
        ///
        /// println!("Created a new instance of FirstOne: {:?}", x);
        /// ```
        #[derive(Debug)]
        pub struct $tyname {
            pub field1: u8,
            pub field2: u16,
            pub field3: u32,
            pub field4: u64,
        }
    }
}
// Now let's actually generate types:
gen_types!(FirstOne);
gen_types!(SecondOne);
gen_types!(Another);
```
So now we have created three structs with different names, but they all have the exact same
documentation, which is an issue for any structs not called `FirstOne`. That’s where
[ doc_comment!](https://docs.rs/macro.doc_comment.html) macro comes in handy!

Let’s rewrite the `gen_types!` macro:

```
// Of course, we need to import the `doc_comment` macro:
#[macro_use]
extern crate doc_comment;
macro_rules! gen_types {
    ($tyname:ident) => {
        doc_comment! {
concat!("This is a wonderful generated struct!
You can use it as follow:
```
let x = ", stringify!($tyname), " {
    field1: 0,
    field2: 0,
    field3: 0,
    field4: 0,
};
println!(\"Created a new instance of ", stringify!($tyname), ": {:?}\", x);
```"),
            #[derive(Debug)]
            pub struct $tyname {
                pub field1: u8,
                pub field2: u16,
                pub field3: u32,
                pub field4: u64,
            }
        }
    }
}
gen_types!(FirstOne);
gen_types!(SecondOne);
gen_types!(Another);
```
Now each struct has doc which match itself!

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [doc_](https://docs.rs/macro.doc_comment.html)- comment
- This macro can be used to generate documentation upon a type/item (or just to test outer markdown file code examples).
- [doctest](https://docs.rs/macro.doctest.html)
- This macro provides a simpler way to test an outer markdown file.

---

# tempdir - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tempdir/^0.3/

## Expand description

Temporary directories of files.

The [ TempDir](https://docs.rs/struct.TempDir.html) type creates a directory on the file system that
is deleted once it goes out of scope. At construction, the

`TempDir` creates a new directory with a randomly generated name
and a prefix of your choosing.[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
extern crate tempdir;
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{self, Write};
use tempdir::TempDir;
fn main() {
    if let Err(_) = run() {
        ::std::process::exit(1);
    }
}
fn run() -> Result<(), io::Error> {
    // Create a directory inside of `std::env::temp_dir()`, named with
    // the prefix "example".
    let tmp_dir = TempDir::new("example")?;
    let file_path = tmp_dir.path().join("my-temporary-note.txt");
    let mut tmp_file = File::create(file_path)?;
    writeln!(tmp_file, "Brian was here. Briefly.")?;
    // By closing the `TempDir` explicitly, we can check that it has
    // been deleted successfully. If we don't close it explicitly,
    // the directory will still be deleted when `tmp_dir` goes out
    // of scope, but we won't know whether deleting the directory
    // succeeded.
    drop(tmp_file);
    tmp_dir.close()?;
    Ok(())
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [TempDir](https://docs.rs/struct.TempDir.html)
- A directory in the filesystem that is automatically deleted when it goes out of scope.

---

Support for matching file paths against Unix shell style patterns.

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

---

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (4c9d2bfe4 2026-07-01)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |

# Releases - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/releases

axon-lang-2.34.0

AXON — the formal cognitive language: a deterministic, proof-carrying AI runtime. Native Rust lexer/parser/type-checker/IR generator (re-exported from axon-frontend) plus the runtime: typed channels (π-calculus mobility, capability extrusion), algebraic effects via Free Monad CPS handlers, lease kernel + reconcile loop, the Epistemic Security Kernel, Trust Types, Proof-Carrying Code (independently verifiable proof objects), and the closed-catalog extension mechanism. Crate publishes as `axon-lang`; library import is `use axon::*` so existing call sites keep working unchanged.

# tytanic_filter - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tytanic-filter/0.4.0/tytanic_filter/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#tytanic-filter)`tytanic-filter`

Filtering Tytanic test suites effectively.

This crates provides default implementations for the [ Filter](https://docs.rs/tytanic-core/0.4.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tytanic_core/filter/trait.Filter.html) trait, these
filters are used in the Tytanic CLI.

[§](https://docs.rs#exact-filter-sets)Exact Filter Sets

Exact filter sets can be turned into [ ExactFilter](https://docs.rs/exact/struct.ExactFilter.html), being an exact filter
means they emit errors when expected tests are missing once

[is called.](https://docs.rs/tytanic-core/0.4.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tytanic_core/filter/trait.FilterState.html#method.finish)

`FilterState::finish`[§](https://docs.rs#test-set-expressions)Test Set Expressions

Tests sets are expressions in a set-based DSL for filtering tests according to their identifiers, attributes, and annotations.

Test sets can be parsed and evaluated into an [ ExpressionFilter](https://docs.rs/test_set/struct.ExpressionFilter.html), unlike
explicit filters these are purely additive, i.e. missing tests do not cause
an error.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Combined](https://docs.rs/struct.CombinedFilter.html)- Filter
- A combined exact and test set expression filter.
- [Combined](https://docs.rs/struct.CombinedFilterState.html)- Filter - State
- Created by `Filter::state``CombinedFilter`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Returned by `FilterState::filter``FilterState::finish``CombinedFilterState`

# tytanic 0.4.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/tytanic/0.4.0

# Tytanic

`tytanic` is a test runner for [Typst](https://typst.app) projects.
It helps you worry less about regressions and speeds up your development.

## Features

Out of the box `tytanic` supports the following features:

- compile and compare tests
- manage tests of various types
- manage and update reference documents when tests change
- filter tests effectively for concise test runs

## Documentation

To see how to get started with `tytanic`, check out the [book](https://typst-community.github.io/tytanic/index.html).

## Contribution

[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://docs.rs/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) contains some guidelines for contributing.

## Changelog

The changelog can be found [here](https://docs.rs/docs/CHANGELOG.md).

## License

Tytanic is dual-licensed under MIT or Apache 2.0 (`SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0`).

---

# axon - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/axon-lang/2.34.0/axon/

## Expand description

AXON runtime library — exposes the full AXON runtime: compiler
frontend (re-exported from `axon-frontend`), handlers, runtime
primitives, ESK, HTTP/WebSocket servers, persistence, OTS pipelines.

Used by the `axon` binary and by integration tests.

[§](https://docs.rs#frontend-vs-runtime)Frontend vs runtime

§Fase 12.a — the compiler frontend (lexer, parser, AST, type checker,
IR generator, top-level checker, and the closed catalogs used by the
type checker) lives in the sibling crate `axon-frontend`, which has
zero runtime dependencies. This crate re-exports those modules
transparently so every existing caller (76 call sites across 26
files) keeps compiling without changes. The crate `axon-lsp`
consumes `axon-frontend` directly, skipping the runtime surface.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [advantage_](https://docs.rs/advantage_witness/index.html)- witness
- §Fase 69.a — the Advantage Witness: a transversal law
(`axon://logic/no_unwitnessed_advantage`). A primitive may not claim an advantage over a cheaper baseline without a machine-checkable witness on real data; the`AdvantageWitness`trait + closed metric catalog + verdict. §Fase 69.a — The Advantage Witness: a transversal Axon law.
- [anchor_](https://docs.rs/anchor_checker/index.html)- checker
- Anchor runtime checkers — validate LLM output against AXON anchor constraints.
- [api_](https://docs.rs/api_keys/index.html)- keys
- API Key Management — multi-tenant key registry for AxonServer.
- [ast](https://docs.rs/ast/index.html)
- AXON AST node definitions — direct port of axon/compiler/ast_nodes.py.

The static algebra (`axon_frontend::session`: duality, regular-coinductive equality, credit-refined backpressure index`!ⁿA.S`) gets a dynamic counterpart here: an operational state machine (`SessionRuntime`) with one method per algebra rule, a wire envelope (`Frame`), and an RFC 6455 WebSocket carrier (`ws::drive`) that runs a session type against a peer. Carrier-agnostic core; the WS layer is one binding. §Fase 41.d — the**runtime**of a session-typed dialogue.

# axon_emcp - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/axon-emcp/0.20.0/axon_emcp/

## Expand description

`axon-emcp` — the official ℰMCP (Epistemic Model Context Protocol)
server for AXON, exposed as a library so integration tests under
`tests/` can drive the same `compiler_pipeline` and `knowledge`
surfaces the `main` binary uses at runtime.

The binary entrypoint lives in `src/main.rs`; everything callable
from outside the crate (tests, future embedders) goes through the
re-exports here. Keeping a hybrid bin+lib crate avoids duplicating
module bodies and ensures the in-binary code path and the
integration-test code path compile from the exact same source.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [compiler_](https://docs.rs/compiler_pipeline/index.html)- pipeline
- The lex → parse → type-check → IR-generate pipeline, projected through a single structured-diagnostic shape.
- [compose](https://docs.rs/compose/index.html)
- `axon.compose(intent)`— natural-language brief → typed scaffold.
- [knowledge](https://docs.rs/knowledge/index.html)
- The knowledge base catalogue.
- [otlp](https://docs.rs/otlp/index.html)
- §Fase 10 — OTLP/gRPC exporter follow-up to the §Fase 8 telemetry surface.
- [prompts](https://docs.rs/prompts/index.html)
- MCP prompts — parameterized prompt templates the host surfaces to the human user as named recipes (slash-commands, chat-menu entries, prompt pickers).
- [resources](https://docs.rs/resources/index.html)
- MCP resources the connected agent can read by URI.
- [scaffold](https://docs.rs/scaffold/index.html)
- `axon-emcp scaffold-primitive <name>`— stamp a markdown skeleton for one primitive’s documentation, with frontmatter pre-populated from the canonical- `PRIMITIVE_REGISTRY`
- [server](https://docs.rs/server/index.html)
- MCP protocol over stdio + JSON-RPC 2.0.
- [telemetry](https://docs.rs/telemetry/index.html)
- §Fase 8 — Telemetry surface, OTLP-grade in shape + privacy-first by construction.
- [tools](https://docs.rs/tools/index.html)
- MCP tools the connected agent can invoke.

# mer-iot 0.0.6 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/mer-iot/0.0.6

# iot-data-generator (`mer`)

A developer-friendly IoT test data generator CLI written in Rust.

Generate realistic IoT sensor payloads and send them to your system over **MQTT**, **HTTP**, or **TCP** — with zero infrastructure required to get started.

This is not a load-testing tool.It is focused on high-quality, realistic IoT test data.

## Demo

From setup to sending data over MQTT:

## Features

- **Random payload**generation — temperature, humidity, voltage, current, power, energy, status
- **Custom Handlebars templates**— full control over payload structure
- **Three protocols**— MQTT (plain & TLS), HTTP, TCP
- **Authentication**— username/password, Bearer token, API key header
- **Environment variable expansion**— keep secrets out of config files with- `${VAR_NAME}`
- **Validation & preview**— check config and see sample payloads before sending
- **Run control**— total message count, interval, or hard time limit
- **Cross-platform**— Linux, macOS, Windows (prebuilt binaries available)
- **Docker ready**— single image, compose with a local Mosquitto broker included

## Installation

### Option 1 — crates.io (recommended)

Install the latest release straight from [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/mer-iot) with Cargo (installs the `mer` binary):

```
```
Requires [Rust](https://rustup.rs/) (stable). Upgrade later with `cargo install mer-iot --force`.

### Option 2 — Prebuilt binary

Download the latest binary for your platform from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/iotmertech/iot-data-generator/releases). Binaries are built automatically when a [release is published](https://github.com/iotmertech/iot-data-generator/releases):

```
# Linux x86_64
 |
# Linux ARM64
 |
# macOS Apple Silicon
 |
# macOS Intel
 |
# Windows (PowerShell)
# Add mer.exe to your PATH
```
### Option 3 — Build from source

Requires [Rust](https://rustup.rs/) (stable):

```
# Binary: ./target/release/mer
```
### Option 4 — Docker

```
# Pull and run (no local Rust needed)
# Run an example against a local broker
```
### Option 5 — Docker Compose (bring your own broker)

Runs `mer` in a container and connects to your existing broker:

```
```
For brokers that require auth, edit the `command` in `docker-compose.yml` to use `docker/mer.docker-auth.yaml` and fill in `MQTT_USERNAME` / `MQTT_PASSWORD` in your `.env`.

No broker is bundled —

`mer`connects to whatever broker you point it at.

## Quickstart

### 1. Generate a starter config

```
```
On Windows, prefer `-f` over shell redirection (`> mer.yaml`). PowerShell writes UTF-16 by default, which older `mer` versions could not read.

### 2. Preview payloads

```
```
### 3. Validate the config

```
```
### 4. Send data

```
```
## Commands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `mer init --protocol <mqtt | http |
| `mer validate config -f <file>` | Validate a config file (exits 0 on success) |
| `mer preview payload -f <file> [-n N]` | Preview N generated payloads (default 3) |
| `mer mqtt run -f <file>` | Send MQTT messages |
| `mer http run -f <file>` | Send HTTP requests |
| `mer tcp run -f <file>` | Send TCP messages |

## Config Reference

### MQTT

```
protocol: mqtt
target:
  broker: "mqtt://mqtt.iotmer.cloud:1883"     # or mqtts:// for TLS (port 8883)
  topic: "devices/{device_id}/telemetry"
  client_id: "mer-{device_id}"        # optional, auto-generated if omitted
  qos: 1                              # 0, 1, or 2
  retain: false
device:
  count: 5
  id_prefix: device                   # device IDs: device-0000, device-0001, …
payload:
  mode: random                        # or template
run:
  total_messages: 100
  interval_ms: 1000                   # ms between messages
  duration_secs: 60                   # optional hard time limit
```
### HTTP

```
protocol: http
target:
  url: "http://ingest.iotmer.cloud:8080/api/v1/devices/{device_id}/data"
  method: POST                        # GET, POST, PUT, PATCH
  timeout_secs: 10
  headers:
    Content-Type: "application/json"
    X-Custom-Header: "value"
device:
  count: 3
  id_prefix: sensor
payload:
  mode: random
run:
  total_messages: 50
  interval_ms: 500
```
### TCP

```
protocol: tcp
target:
  host: localhost
  port: 9000
  timeout_secs: 5
  line_delimiter: true                # append \n to each message
device:
  count: 2
  id_prefix: node
payload:
  mode: random
run:
  total_messages: 20
  interval_ms: 1000
```
## Simulated Timestamps

By default each payload's timestamp is the current wall-clock time. Add an
optional `time` section to generate a **simulated clock** instead — useful for
backfilling historical data or producing deterministic, evenly-spaced series.

```
time:
  mode: fixed                    # real | fixed | random   (default: real)
  start: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"  # also accepts "2026-01-01 00:00:00" (UTC)
  step_secs: 300                 # fixed mode: +5 min per message
  min_secs: 60                   # random mode: minimum +1 min
  max_secs: 1800                 # random mode: maximum +30 min
  field: ts                      # JSON key for the timestamp (default "ts")
```
- `real`
- `fixed`- `start + seq * step_secs`. Deterministic and evenly spaced (e.g. start at- `2026-01-01 00:00:00`, then- `00:05:00`,- `00:10:00`, …).
- `random`- `start`, then advances by a random amount between- `min_secs`and- `max_secs`for each message.

The clock is global and advances once per message (in the same order as the
`seq` counter), shared across all devices.

In `template` mode the simulated timestamp is available as `{{ts}}` (RFC3339).
`{{now_utc}}` always returns real wall-clock time regardless of the `time`
setting.

## Payload Modes

`random` (default)

Generates a realistic IoT JSON payload automatically:

```
```
Field ranges:

| Field | Range |
|---|---|
| `temperature` | 15.0 – 45.0 °C |
| `humidity` | 20.0 – 95.0 % |
| `voltage` | 220.0 – 240.0 V |
| `current` | 0.1 – 15.0 A |
| `power` | 10.0 – 3600.0 W |
| `energy_total` | 0.0 – 10000.0 kWh |
| `status` | `online`(4/6),`offline`(1/6),`error`(1/6) |

`template`

```
payload:
  mode: template
  template_inline: |
    {
      "device_id": "{{device_id}}",
      "ts": "{{now_utc}}",
      "temperature": {{random_float 18.0 35.0}},
      "humidity": {{random_float 30.0 90.0}},
      "active": {{random_bool}},
      "seq": {{seq}},
      "level": {{random_int 0 5}}
    }
```
Or load from an external file:

```
payload:
  mode: template
  template_file: ./my-template.json
```
#### Template helpers

| Helper | Example | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `{{now_utc}}` | — | `2024-01-01T12:00:00Z` |
| `{{ts}}` | — | simulated time (see `time`config) |
| `{{random_int min max}}` | `{{random_int 0 100}}` | `42` |
| `{{random_float min max}}` | `{{random_float 10.0 50.0}}` | `27.35` |
| `{{random_bool}}` | — | `true`or`false` |
| `{{device_id}}` | — | `sensor-0003` |
| `{{device.index}}` | — | `3` |
| `{{seq}}` | — | `17` |
| `{{seq_pulse min max peak_at total_steps}}` | `{{seq_pulse 8.0 90.0 1344 2688}}` | triangle: `min`at edges,`max`at`peak_at` |
| `{{seq_inv_pulse min max peak_at total_steps}}` | `{{seq_inv_pulse 0.80 0.99 1344 2688}}` | inverted triangle: `max`at edges,`min`at`peak_at` |
| `{{seq_after offset scale}}` | `{{seq_after 1344 0.5}}` | delayed ramp: `max(0, seq - offset) * scale` |
| `{{seq_pulse_rand min max peak_min peak_max total_steps}}` | `{{seq_pulse_rand 8.0 90.0 1000 1700 2688}}` | triangle with a randompeak in`[peak_min, peak_max]`(stable per device) |
| `{{seq_inv_pulse_rand min max peak_min peak_max total_steps}}` | `{{seq_inv_pulse_rand 0.80 0.99 1000 1700 2688}}` | inverted triangle sharing the device's random peak |
| `{{seq_cum_energy step_min step_max peak_at total_steps [readings_per_day]}}` | `{{seq_cum_energy 2.0 18.0 1344 2688 48}}` | monotonic cumulative energy (kWh / kVArh); daily increments vary |

The `seq_*` helpers read the current message `seq` (and device index)
automatically from the context — you don't pass them as arguments. They're handy
for shaping values over a run (e.g. a mid-cycle triangle load, a cos φ dip,
cumulative energy registers, or a compensation bank that starts accumulating after
a threshold).

Use the `_rand` variants when each device should peak at a **different, random
time**: the peak is drawn once from `[peak_min, peak_max]` and stays fixed for
that device's whole run. All `_rand` helpers for a given device share the same
peak, so active/reactive load and the cos φ dip line up in time. See
[ energy-triangle.yaml](https://docs.rs/examples/energy-triangle.yaml).

## Authentication

### Username / Password (MQTT, HTTP)

```
auth:
  type: username_password
  username: myuser
  password: "${MQTT_PASSWORD}"
```
For MQTT, you can also set credentials directly under `target`:

```
target:
  broker: "mqtts://mqtt.iotmer.cloud:8883"
  topic: "test/{device_id}"
  auth:
    username: myuser
    password: "${MQTT_PASSWORD}"
```
### Bearer Token (HTTP)

```
auth:
  type: bearer
  token: "${API_TOKEN}"
```
### API Key Header (HTTP)

```
auth:
  type: api_key
  header: X-API-Key
  value: "${API_KEY}"
```
## Environment Variables

Use `${VAR_NAME}` anywhere in your config to inject secrets at runtime:

```
auth:
  type: bearer
  token: "${MY_API_TOKEN}"
```
```
```
If a variable is not set, `mer` exits with a clear error:

```
Error: Environment variable 'MY_API_TOKEN' is not set
```
## Run Summary

After each run, `mer` prints a summary:

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  Run Summary — MQTT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  Total sent    : 100
  Successful    : 98
  Failed        : 2
  Success rate  : 98.0%
  Errors        : 2
  Bytes sent    : 24.5 KB
  Elapsed       : 100.12s
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
```
## Examples

The `[examples/](examples/)` directory contains ready-to-use configs:

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `[mqtt-basic.yaml](examples/mqtt-basic.yaml)` | 5 devices, 20 messages, random payload, MQTT localhost |
| `[demo-mqtt.yaml](examples/demo-mqtt.yaml)` | Demo: mqtt.iotmer.cloud, public broker, README GIF |
| `[mqtt-auth.yaml](examples/mqtt-auth.yaml)` | MQTT with username/password auth |
| `[mqtt-tls.yaml](examples/mqtt-tls.yaml)` | MQTT over TLS ( `mqtts://`) with auth |
| `[http-basic.yaml](examples/http-basic.yaml)` | 3 sensors, HTTP POST with custom header |
| `[http-bearer.yaml](examples/http-bearer.yaml)` | HTTP POST with Bearer token auth |
| `[http-api-key.yaml](examples/http-api-key.yaml)` | HTTP POST with API key header auth |
| `[tcp-basic.yaml](examples/tcp-basic.yaml)` | 2 nodes, TCP with line delimiter |
| `[custom-template.yaml](examples/custom-template.yaml)` | MQTT with inline Handlebars template |
| `[smart-home.yaml](examples/smart-home.yaml)` | Smart home sensors (temp, plug, door, CO₂, lux) |
| `[industrial.yaml](examples/industrial.yaml)` | Factory floor machines (vibration, pressure, flow, RPM) |
| `[fleet-tracking.yaml](examples/fleet-tracking.yaml)` | Vehicle GPS tracking over HTTP |
| `[energy-meter.yaml](examples/energy-meter.yaml)` | Three-phase smart energy meters over MQTT |
| `[weather-station.yaml](examples/weather-station.yaml)` | Weather stations over TCP (wind, rain, UV, pressure) |
| `[duration-limited.yaml](examples/duration-limited.yaml)` | Time-capped run with `duration_secs` |
| `[time-fixed.yaml](examples/time-fixed.yaml)` | Simulated timestamps, fixed +5 min step |
| `[time-random.yaml](examples/time-random.yaml)` | Simulated timestamps, random 1–30 min step |
| `[time-template.yaml](examples/time-template.yaml)` | Simulated `{{ts}}`inside a custom template |
| `[energy-triangle.yaml](examples/energy-triangle.yaml)` | Mid-month triangle load, cos φ dip & compensation ramp |

## Security

Please read our [Security Policy](https://docs.rs/SECURITY.md) before reporting vulnerabilities.

**Key points:**

- Never commit plaintext secrets — use `${ENV_VAR}`in config files
- Use `mqtts://`for production MQTT connections
- Use `https://`for production HTTP endpoints

# sequenceprofiler 0.5.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sequenceprofiler/0.5.0

sequenceprofiler-0.5.0 is not a library.

                # sequenceprofiler

- This crate has the following features: fasta file should be a linear fasta and not a multi line fasta just like long-read.
- Sequence, which allows based on the similarity of the shared unique kmers and also allows for the filtering of the sequences so that you can build a native index graph faster.
- SequenceSeq, which allows for the sequence similarity on a sequence to next iter sequence.
- longread: finding the origin of the kmers.Back to sequences:Find the origin of 𝑘-mers DOI: 10.21105/joss.07066. Output a table for the direct ingestion into any graphs. Outputs a sam type file with the distinct count of the kmers and can be used for the jellyfish count.Support both the genome and the longread fasta file.
- Jellyfish: a rust implementation of the jellyfish for the counts.Outputs both the unique counts, all counts.It will produce allkmers, uniquekmers, countkmers

```
cargo build
```

# glob 0.3.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/glob/0.3.3

# glob

Support for matching file paths against Unix shell style patterns.

## Usage

To use `glob`, add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "0.3.2"
```
If you're using Rust 1.30 or earlier, or edition 2015, add this to your crate root:

```
extern crate glob;
```
## Examples

Print all jpg files in /media/ and all of its subdirectories.

```
use glob;
for entry in glob.expect
```

# glob 0.3.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/glob/0.3.3/source/

#
                    glob 0.3.3

                Support for matching file paths against Unix shell style patterns.

---

# glob - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/glob/0.3.3/target-redirect/glob/

## Expand description

Support for matching file paths against Unix shell style patterns.

The `glob` and `glob_with` functions allow querying the filesystem for all
files that match a particular pattern (similar to the libc `glob` function).
The methods on the `Pattern` type provide functionality for checking if
individual paths match a particular pattern (similar to the libc `fnmatch`
function).

For consistency across platforms, and for Windows support, this module
is implemented entirely in Rust rather than deferring to the libc
`glob`/`fnmatch` functions.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

To print all jpg files in `/media/` and all of its subdirectories.

```
use glob::glob;
for entry in glob("/media/**/*.jpg").expect("Failed to read glob pattern") {
    match entry {
        Ok(path) => println!("{:?}", path.display()),
        Err(e) => println!("{:?}", e),
    }
}
```
To print all files containing the letter “a”, case insensitive, in a `local`
directory relative to the current working directory. This ignores errors
instead of printing them.

```
use glob::glob_with;
use glob::MatchOptions;
let options = MatchOptions {
    case_sensitive: false,
    require_literal_separator: false,
    require_literal_leading_dot: false,
};
for entry in glob_with("local/*a*", options).unwrap() {
    if let Ok(path) = entry {
        println!("{:?}", path.display())
    }
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Glob](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobError.html)- Error
- A glob iteration error.
- [Match](https://docs.rs/struct.MatchOptions.html)- Options
- Configuration options to modify the behaviour of `Pattern::matches_with(..)`.
- [Paths](https://docs.rs/struct.Paths.html)
- An iterator that yields `Path`s from the filesystem that match a particular pattern.
- [Pattern](https://docs.rs/struct.Pattern.html)
- A compiled Unix shell style pattern.
- [Pattern](https://docs.rs/struct.PatternError.html)- Error
- A pattern parsing error.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [glob](https://docs.rs/fn.glob.html)
- Return an iterator that produces all the `Path`s that match the given pattern using default match options, which may be absolute or relative to the current working directory.
- [glob_](https://docs.rs/fn.glob_with.html)- with
- Return an iterator that produces all the `Path`s that match the given pattern using the specified match options, which may be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Glob](https://docs.rs/type.GlobResult.html)- Result
- An alias for a glob iteration result.

---

[168](#168)pub fn glob_with(pattern: &str, options: MatchOptions) -> Result<Paths, PatternError> {
[182](#182)    #[cfg(windows)]
[183](#183)    fn check_windows_verbatim(p: &Path) -> bool {
[184](#184)        match p.components().next() {
[185](#185)            Some(Component::Prefix(ref p)) => {
[186](#186)                p.kind().is_verbatim()
[188](#188)                    && if let std::path::Prefix::VerbatimDisk(_) = p.kind() {
[189](#189)                        false
[190](#190)                    } else {
[191](#191)                        true
[192](#192)                    }
[193](#193)            }
[194](#194)            _ => false,
[195](#195)        }
[196](#196)    }
[197](#197)    #[cfg(not(windows))]
[198](#198)    fn check_windows_verbatim(_: &Path) -> bool {
[199](#199)        false
[200](#200)    }
[201](#201)
[202](#202)    #[cfg(windows)]
[203](#203)    fn to_scope(p: &Path) -> PathBuf {
[204](#204)        p.to_path_buf()
[206](#206)    }
[207](#207)    #[cfg(not(windows))]
[208](#208)    fn to_scope(p: &Path) -> PathBuf {
[209](#209)        p.to_path_buf()
[210](#210)    }
[211](#211)
[212](#212)    let _ = Pattern::new(pattern)?;
[214](#214)
[215](#215)    let mut components = Path::new(pattern).components().peekable();
[216](#216)    loop {
[217](#217)        match components.peek() {
[218](#218)            Some(&Component::Prefix(..)) | Some(&Component::RootDir) => {
[219](#219)                components.next();
[220](#220)            }
[221](#221)            _ => break,
[222](#222)        }
[223](#223)    }
[224](#224)    let rest = components.map(|s| s.as_os_str()).collect::<PathBuf>();
[225](#225)    let normalized_pattern = Path::new(pattern).iter().collect::<PathBuf>();
[226](#226)    let root_len = normalized_pattern.to_str().unwrap().len() - rest.to_str().unwrap().len();
[227](#227)    let root = if root_len > 0 {
[228](#228)        Some(Path::new(&pattern[..root_len]))
[229](#229)    } else {
[230](#230)        None
[231](#231)    };
[232](#232)
[233](#233)    if root_len > 0 && check_windows_verbatim(root.unwrap()) {
[234](#234)        return Ok(Paths {
[238](#238)            dir_patterns: Vec::new(),
[239](#239)            require_dir: false,
[240](#240)            options,
[241](#241)            todo: Vec::new(),
[242](#242)            scope: None,
[243](#243)        });
[244](#244)    }
[245](#245)
[246](#246)    let scope = root.map_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("."), to_scope);
[247](#247)    let scope = PathWrapper::from_path(scope);
[248](#248)
[249](#249)    let mut dir_patterns = Vec::new();
[250](#250)    let components =
[251](#251)        pattern[cmp::min(root_len, pattern.len())..].split_terminator(path::is_separator);
[252](#252)
[253](#253)    for component in components {
[254](#254)        dir_patterns.push(Pattern::new(component)?);
[255](#255)    }
[256](#256)
[257](#257)    if root_len == pattern.len() {
[258](#258)        dir_patterns.push(Pattern {
[259](#259)            original: "".to_string(),
[260](#260)            tokens: Vec::new(),
[261](#261)            is_recursive: false,
[262](#262)            has_metachars: false,
[263](#263)        });
[264](#264)    }
[265](#265)
[266](#266)    let last_is_separator = pattern.chars().next_back().map(path::is_separator);
[267](#267)    let require_dir = last_is_separator == Some(true);
[268](#268)    let todo = Vec::new();
[269](#269)
[270](#270)    Ok(Paths {
[271](#271)        dir_patterns,
[272](#272)        require_dir,
[273](#273)        options,
[274](#274)        todo,
[275](#275)        scope: Some(scope),
[276](#276)    })
[277](#277)}

[336](#336)impl PathWrapper {
[337](#337)    fn from_dir_entry(path: PathBuf, e: DirEntry) -> Self {
[338](#338)        let is_directory = e
[339](#339)            .file_type()
[340](#340)            .ok()
[341](#341)            .and_then(|file_type| {
[342](#342)                if file_type.is_symlink() {
[345](#345)                    None
[346](#346)                } else {
[347](#347)                    Some(file_type.is_dir())
[348](#348)                }
[349](#349)            })
[350](#350)            .or_else(|| fs::metadata(&path).map(|m| m.is_dir()).ok())
[351](#351)            .unwrap_or(false);
[352](#352)        Self { path, is_directory }
[353](#353)    }
[354](#354)    fn from_path(path: PathBuf) -> Self {
[355](#355)        let is_directory = fs::metadata(&path).map(|m| m.is_dir()).unwrap_or(false);
[356](#356)        Self { path, is_directory }
[357](#357)    }
[358](#358)

[361](#361)    }

[378](#378)pub type GlobResult = Result<PathBuf, GlobError>;
[383](#383)
[384](#384)impl Iterator for Paths {
[385](#385)    type Item = GlobResult;
[386](#386)
[387](#387)    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<GlobResult> {
[388](#388)        if let Some(scope) = self.scope.take() {
[393](#393)            if !self.dir_patterns.is_empty() {
[394](#394)                assert!(self.dir_patterns.len() < usize::MAX);
[396](#396)
[397](#397)                fill_todo(&mut self.todo, &self.dir_patterns, 0, &scope, self.options);
[398](#398)            }
[399](#399)        }
[400](#400)
[401](#401)        loop {
[402](#402)            if self.dir_patterns.is_empty() || self.todo.is_empty() {
[403](#403)                return None;
[404](#404)            }
[405](#405)
[406](#406)            let (path, mut idx) = match self.todo.pop().unwrap() {
[407](#407)                Ok(pair) => pair,
[408](#408)                Err(e) => return Some(Err(e)),
[409](#409)            };
[410](#410)
[411](#411)            if idx == usize::MAX {
[414](#414)                if self.require_dir && !path.is_directory {
[415](#415)                    continue;
[416](#416)                }
[417](#417)                return Some(Ok(path.into_path()));
[418](#418)            }
[419](#419)
[420](#420)            if self.dir_patterns[idx].is_recursive {
[421](#421)                let mut next = idx;
[422](#422)
[423](#423)                while (next + 1) < self.dir_patterns.len()
[425](#425)                    && self.dir_patterns[next + 1].is_recursive
[426](#426)                {
[427](#427)                    next += 1;
[428](#428)                }
[429](#429)
[430](#430)                if path.is_directory {
[431](#431)                    fill_todo(
[435](#435)                        &mut self.todo,
[436](#436)                        &self.dir_patterns,
[437](#437)                        next,
[438](#438)                        &path,
[439](#439)                        self.options,
[440](#440)                    );
[441](#441)
[442](#442)                    if next == self.dir_patterns.len() - 1 {
[443](#443)                        return Some(Ok(path.into_path()));
[446](#446)                    } else {
[447](#447)                        idx = next + 1;
[449](#449)                    }
[450](#450)                } else if next == self.dir_patterns.len() - 1 {
[451](#451)                    continue;
[454](#454)                } else {
[455](#455)                    idx = next + 1;
[457](#457)                }
[458](#458)            }
[459](#459)
[460](#460)            if self.dir_patterns[idx].matches_with(
[462](#462)                {
[463](#463)                    match path.file_name().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) {
[464](#464)                        None => continue,
[468](#468)                        Some(x) => x,
[469](#469)                    }
[470](#470)                },
[471](#471)                self.options,
[472](#472)            ) {
[473](#473)                if idx == self.dir_patterns.len() - 1 {
[474](#474)                    if !self.require_dir || path.is_directory {
[479](#479)                        return Some(Ok(path.into_path()));
[480](#480)                    }
[481](#481)                } else {
[482](#482)                    fill_todo(
[483](#483)                        &mut self.todo,
[484](#484)                        &self.dir_patterns,
[485](#485)                        idx + 1,
[486](#486)                        &path,
[487](#487)                        self.options,
[488](#488)                    );
[489](#489)                }
[490](#490)            }
[491](#491)        }
[492](#492)    }

[568](#568)impl FromStr for Pattern {

[575](#575)
[576](#576)#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Debug)]
[577](#577)enum PatternToken {
[578](#578)    Char(char),
[579](#579)    AnyChar,
[580](#580)    AnySequence,
[581](#581)    AnyRecursiveSequence,
[582](#582)    AnyWithin(Vec<CharSpecifier>),
[583](#583)    AnyExcept(Vec<CharSpecifier>),
[584](#584)}
[585](#585)
[586](#586)#[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Debug)]
[587](#587)enum CharSpecifier {
[588](#588)    SingleChar(char),
[589](#589)    CharRange(char, char),
[590](#590)}
[591](#591)
[592](#592)#[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq)]
[593](#593)enum MatchResult {
[594](#594)    Match,
[595](#595)    SubPatternDoesntMatch,
[596](#596)    EntirePatternDoesntMatch,
[597](#597)}
[598](#598)
[599](#599)const ERROR_WILDCARDS: &str = "wildcards are either regular `*` or recursive `**`";
[600](#600)const ERROR_RECURSIVE_WILDCARDS: &str = "recursive wildcards must form a single path \
[601](#601)                                         component";
[602](#602)const ERROR_INVALID_RANGE: &str = "invalid range pattern";
[603](#603)
[604](#604)impl Pattern {
[605](#605)    pub fn new(pattern: &str) -> Result<Self, PatternError> {
[609](#609)        let chars = pattern.chars().collect::<Vec<_>>();
[610](#610)        let mut tokens = Vec::new();
[611](#611)        let mut is_recursive = false;
[612](#612)        let mut has_metachars = false;
[613](#613)        let mut i = 0;
[614](#614)
[615](#615)        while i < chars.len() {
[616](#616)            match chars[i] {
[617](#617)                '?' => {
[618](#618)                    has_metachars = true;
[619](#619)                    tokens.push(AnyChar);
[620](#620)                    i += 1;
[621](#621)                }
[622](#622)                '*' => {
[623](#623)                    has_metachars = true;
[624](#624)
[625](#625)                    let old = i;
[626](#626)
[627](#627)                    while i < chars.len() && chars[i] == '*' {
[628](#628)                        i += 1;
[629](#629)                    }
[630](#630)
[631](#631)                    let count = i - old;
[632](#632)
[633](#633)                    match count.cmp(&2) {
[634](#634)                        Ordering::Greater => {
[635](#635)                            return Err(PatternError {
[636](#636)                                pos: old + 2,
[637](#637)                                msg: ERROR_WILDCARDS,
[638](#638)                            })
[639](#639)                        }
[640](#640)                        Ordering::Equal => {
[641](#641)                            let is_valid = if i == 2 || path::is_separator(chars[i - count - 1]) {
[645](#645)                                if i < chars.len() && path::is_separator(chars[i]) {
[647](#647)                                    i += 1;
[648](#648)                                    true
[649](#649)                                } else if i == chars.len() {
[652](#652)                                    true
[653](#653)                                } else {
[655](#655)                                    return Err(PatternError {
[656](#656)                                        pos: i,
[657](#657)                                        msg: ERROR_RECURSIVE_WILDCARDS,
[658](#658)                                    });
[659](#659)                                }
[660](#660)                            } else {
[662](#662)                                return Err(PatternError {
[663](#663)                                    pos: old - 1,
[664](#664)                                    msg: ERROR_RECURSIVE_WILDCARDS,
[665](#665)                                });
[666](#666)                            };
[667](#667)
[668](#668)                            if is_valid {
[669](#669)                                let tokens_len = tokens.len();
[673](#673)
[674](#674)                                if !(tokens_len > 1
[675](#675)                                    && tokens[tokens_len - 1] == AnyRecursiveSequence)
[676](#676)                                {
[677](#677)                                    is_recursive = true;
[678](#678)                                    tokens.push(AnyRecursiveSequence);
[679](#679)                                }
[680](#680)                            }
[681](#681)                        }
[682](#682)                        Ordering::Less => tokens.push(AnySequence),
[683](#683)                    }
[684](#684)                }
[685](#685)                '[' => {
[686](#686)                    has_metachars = true;
[687](#687)
[688](#688)                    if i + 4 <= chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '!' {
[689](#689)                        match chars[i + 3..].iter().position(|x| *x == ']') {
[690](#690)                            None => (),
[691](#691)                            Some(j) => {
[692](#692)                                let chars = &chars[i + 2..i + 3 + j];
[693](#693)                                let cs = parse_char_specifiers(chars);
[694](#694)                                tokens.push(AnyExcept(cs));
[695](#695)                                i += j + 4;
[696](#696)                                continue;
[697](#697)                            }
[698](#698)                        }
[699](#699)                    } else if i + 3 <= chars.len() && chars[i + 1] != '!' {
[700](#700)                        match chars[i + 2..].iter().position(|x| *x == ']') {
[701](#701)                            None => (),
[702](#702)                            Some(j) => {
[703](#703)                                let cs = parse_char_specifiers(&chars[i + 1..i + 2 + j]);
[704](#704)                                tokens.push(AnyWithin(cs));
[705](#705)                                i += j + 3;
[706](#706)                                continue;
[707](#707)                            }
[708](#708)                        }
[709](#709)                    }
[710](#710)
[711](#711)                    return Err(PatternError {
[713](#713)                        pos: i,
[714](#714)                        msg: ERROR_INVALID_RANGE,
[715](#715)                    });
[716](#716)                }
[717](#717)                c => {
[718](#718)                    tokens.push(Char(c));
[719](#719)                    i += 1;
[720](#720)                }
[721](#721)            }
[722](#722)        }
[723](#723)
[724](#724)        Ok(Self {
[725](#725)            tokens,
[726](#726)            original: pattern.to_string(),
[727](#727)            is_recursive,
[728](#728)            has_metachars,
[729](#729)        })
[730](#730)    }
[731](#731)
[732](#732)    pub fn escape(s: &str) -> String {
[736](#736)        let mut escaped = String::new();
[737](#737)        for c in s.chars() {
[738](#738)            match c {
[739](#739)                '?' | '*' | '[' | ']' => {
[742](#742)                    escaped.push('[');
[743](#743)                    escaped.push(c);
[744](#744)                    escaped.push(']');
[745](#745)                }
[746](#746)                c => {
[747](#747)                    escaped.push(c);
[748](#748)                }
[749](#749)            }
[750](#750)        }
[751](#751)        escaped
[752](#752)    }
[753](#753)
[754](#754)    pub fn matches(&self, str: &str) -> bool {
[767](#767)        self.matches_with(str, MatchOptions::new())
[768](#768)    }
[769](#769)
[770](#770)    pub fn matches_path(&self, path: &Path) -> bool {
[773](#773)        path.to_str().map_or(false, |s| self.matches(s))
[775](#775)    }
[776](#776)
[777](#777)    pub fn matches_with(&self, str: &str, options: MatchOptions) -> bool {
[780](#780)        self.matches_from(true, str.chars(), 0, options) == Match
[781](#781)    }
[782](#782)
[783](#783)    pub fn matches_path_with(&self, path: &Path, options: MatchOptions) -> bool {
[786](#786)        path.to_str()
[788](#788)            .map_or(false, |s| self.matches_with(s, options))
[789](#789)    }
[790](#790)
[791](#791)    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str {
[793](#793)        &self.original
[794](#794)    }
[795](#795)
[796](#796)    fn matches_from(
[797](#797)        &self,
[798](#798)        mut follows_separator: bool,
[799](#799)        mut file: std::str::Chars,
[800](#800)        i: usize,
[801](#801)        options: MatchOptions,
[802](#802)    ) -> MatchResult {
[803](#803)        for (ti, token) in self.tokens[i..].iter().enumerate() {
[804](#804)            match *token {
[805](#805)                AnySequence | AnyRecursiveSequence => {
[806](#806)                    debug_assert!(match *token {
[808](#808)                        AnyRecursiveSequence => follows_separator,
[809](#809)                        _ => true,
[810](#810)                    });
[811](#811)
[812](#812)                    match self.matches_from(follows_separator, file.clone(), i + ti + 1, options) {
[814](#814)                        SubPatternDoesntMatch => (), m => return m,
[816](#816)                    };
[817](#817)
[818](#818)                    while let Some(c) = file.next() {
[819](#819)                        if follows_separator && options.require_literal_leading_dot && c == '.' {
[820](#820)                            return SubPatternDoesntMatch;
[821](#821)                        }
[822](#822)                        follows_separator = path::is_separator(c);
[823](#823)                        match *token {
[824](#824)                            AnyRecursiveSequence if !follows_separator => continue,
[825](#825)                            AnySequence
[826](#826)                                if options.require_literal_separator && follows_separator =>
[827](#827)                            {
[828](#828)                                return SubPatternDoesntMatch
[829](#829)                            }
[830](#830)                            _ => (),
[831](#831)                        }
[832](#832)                        match self.matches_from(
[833](#833)                            follows_separator,
[834](#834)                            file.clone(),
[835](#835)                            i + ti + 1,
[836](#836)                            options,
[837](#837)                        ) {
[838](#838)                            SubPatternDoesntMatch => (), m => return m,
[840](#840)                        }
[841](#841)                    }
[842](#842)                }
[843](#843)                _ => {
[844](#844)                    let c = match file.next() {
[845](#845)                        Some(c) => c,
[846](#846)                        None => return EntirePatternDoesntMatch,
[847](#847)                    };
[848](#848)
[849](#849)                    let is_sep = path::is_separator(c);
[850](#850)
[851](#851)                    if !match *token {
[852](#852)                        AnyChar | AnyWithin(..) | AnyExcept(..)
[853](#853)                            if (options.require_literal_separator && is_sep)
[854](#854)                                || (follows_separator
[855](#855)                                    && options.require_literal_leading_dot
[856](#856)                                    && c == '.') =>
[857](#857)                        {
[858](#858)                            false
[859](#859)                        }
[860](#860)                        AnyChar => true,
[861](#861)                        AnyWithin(ref specifiers) => in_char_specifiers(specifiers, c, options),
[862](#862)                        AnyExcept(ref specifiers) => !in_char_specifiers(specifiers, c, options),
[863](#863)                        Char(c2) => chars_eq(c, c2, options.case_sensitive),
[864](#864)                        AnySequence | AnyRecursiveSequence => unreachable!(),
[865](#865)                    } {
[866](#866)                        return SubPatternDoesntMatch;
[867](#867)                    }
[868](#868)                    follows_separator = is_sep;
[869](#869)                }
[870](#870)            }
[871](#871)        }
[872](#872)
[873](#873)        if file.next().is_none() {
[875](#875)            Match
[876](#876)        } else {
[877](#877)            SubPatternDoesntMatch
[878](#878)        }
[879](#879)    }
[880](#880)}
[881](#881)
[882](#882)fn fill_todo(
[886](#886)    todo: &mut Vec<Result<(PathWrapper, usize), GlobError>>,
[887](#887)    patterns: &[Pattern],
[888](#888)    idx: usize,
[889](#889)    path: &PathWrapper,
[890](#890)    options: MatchOptions,
[891](#891)) {
[892](#892)    let add = |todo: &mut Vec<_>, next_path: PathWrapper| {
[893](#893)        if idx + 1 == patterns.len() {
[894](#894)            todo.push(Ok((next_path, usize::MAX)));
[898](#898)        } else {
[899](#899)            fill_todo(todo, patterns, idx + 1, &next_path, options);
[900](#900)        }
[901](#901)    };
[902](#902)
[903](#903)    let pattern = &patterns[idx];
[904](#904)    let is_dir = path.is_directory;
[905](#905)    let curdir = path.as_ref() == Path::new(".");
[906](#906)    match (pattern.has_metachars, is_dir) {
[907](#907)        (false, _) => {
[908](#908)            debug_assert!(
[909](#909)                pattern
[910](#910)                    .tokens
[911](#911)                    .iter()
[912](#912)                    .all(|tok| matches!(tok, PatternToken::Char(_))),
[913](#913)                "broken invariant: pattern has metachars but shouldn't"
[914](#914)            );
[915](#915)            let s = pattern.as_str();
[916](#916)
[917](#917)            let special = "." == s || ".." == s;
[923](#923)            let next_path = if curdir {
[924](#924)                PathBuf::from(s)
[925](#925)            } else {
[926](#926)                path.join(s)
[927](#927)            };
[928](#928)            let next_path = PathWrapper::from_path(next_path);
[929](#929)            if (special && is_dir)
[930](#930)                || (!special
[931](#931)                    && (fs::metadata(&next_path).is_ok()
[932](#932)                        || fs::symlink_metadata(&next_path).is_ok()))
[933](#933)            {
[934](#934)                add(todo, next_path);
[935](#935)            }
[936](#936)        }
[937](#937)        (true, true) => {
[938](#938)            let dirs = fs::read_dir(path).and_then(|d| {
[939](#939)                d.map(|e| {
[940](#940)                    e.map(|e| {
[941](#941)                        let path = if curdir {
[942](#942)                            PathBuf::from(e.path().file_name().unwrap())
[943](#943)                        } else {
[944](#944)                            e.path()
[945](#945)                        };
[946](#946)                        PathWrapper::from_dir_entry(path, e)
[947](#947)                    })
[948](#948)                })
[949](#949)                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
[950](#950)            });
[951](#951)            match dirs {
[952](#952)                Ok(mut children) => {
[953](#953)                    if options.require_literal_leading_dot {
[954](#954)                        children
[955](#955)                            .retain(|x| !x.file_name().unwrap().to_str().unwrap().starts_with('.'));
[956](#956)                    }
[957](#957)                    children.sort_by(|p1, p2| p2.file_name().cmp(&p1.file_name()));
[958](#958)                    todo.extend(children.into_iter().map(|x| Ok((x, idx))));
[959](#959)
[960](#960)                    if !pattern.tokens.is_empty() && pattern.tokens[0] == Char('.') {
[966](#966)                        for &special in &[".", ".."] {
[967](#967)                            if pattern.matches_with(special, options) {
[968](#968)                                add(todo, PathWrapper::from_path(path.join(special)));
[969](#969)                            }
[970](#970)                        }
[971](#971)                    }
[972](#972)                }
[973](#973)                Err(e) => {
[974](#974)                    todo.push(Err(GlobError {
[975](#975)                        path: path.to_path_buf(),
[976](#976)                        error: e,
[977](#977)                    }));
[978](#978)                }
[979](#979)            }
[980](#980)        }
[981](#981)        (true, false) => {
[982](#982)            }
[984](#984)    }
[985](#985)}
[986](#986)
[987](#987)fn parse_char_specifiers(s: &[char]) -> Vec<CharSpecifier> {
[988](#988)    let mut cs = Vec::new();
[989](#989)    let mut i = 0;
[990](#990)    while i < s.len() {
[991](#991)        if i + 3 <= s.len() && s[i + 1] == '-' {
[992](#992)            cs.push(CharRange(s[i], s[i + 2]));
[993](#993)            i += 3;
[994](#994)        } else {
[995](#995)            cs.push(SingleChar(s[i]));
[996](#996)            i += 1;
[997](#997)        }
[998](#998)    }
[999](#999)    cs
[1000](#1000)}
[1001](#1001)
[1002](#1002)fn in_char_specifiers(specifiers: &[CharSpecifier], c: char, options: MatchOptions) -> bool {
[1003](#1003)    for &specifier in specifiers.iter() {
[1004](#1004)        match specifier {
[1005](#1005)            SingleChar(sc) => {
[1006](#1006)                if chars_eq(c, sc, options.case_sensitive) {
[1007](#1007)                    return true;
[1008](#1008)                }
[1009](#1009)            }
[1010](#1010)            CharRange(start, end) => {
[1011](#1011)                if !options.case_sensitive && c.is_ascii() && start.is_ascii() && end.is_ascii() {
[1013](#1013)                    let start = start.to_ascii_lowercase();
[1014](#1014)                    let end = end.to_ascii_lowercase();
[1015](#1015)
[1016](#1016)                    let start_up = start.to_uppercase().next().unwrap();
[1017](#1017)                    let end_up = end.to_uppercase().next().unwrap();
[1018](#1018)
[1019](#1019)                    if start != start_up && end != end_up {
[1022](#1022)                        let c = c.to_ascii_lowercase();
[1023](#1023)                        if c >= start && c <= end {
[1024](#1024)                            return true;
[1025](#1025)                        }
[1026](#1026)                    }
[1027](#1027)                }
[1028](#1028)
[1029](#1029)                if c >= start && c <= end {
[1030](#1030)                    return true;
[1031](#1031)                }
[1032](#1032)            }
[1033](#1033)        }
[1034](#1034)    }
[1035](#1035)
[1036](#1036)    false
[1037](#1037)}
[1038](#1038)
[1039](#1039)fn chars_eq(a: char, b: char, case_sensitive: bool) -> bool {
[1041](#1041)    if cfg!(windows) && path::is_separator(a) && path::is_separator(b) {
[1042](#1042)        true
[1043](#1043)    } else if !case_sensitive && a.is_ascii() && b.is_ascii() {
[1044](#1044)        a.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&b)
[1046](#1046)    } else {
[1047](#1047)        a == b
[1048](#1048)    }
[1049](#1049)}
[1050](#1050)
[1051](#1051)#[allow(missing_copy_implementations)]
[1053](#1053)#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Default)]
[1054](#1054)pub struct MatchOptions {
[1055](#1055)    pub case_sensitive: bool,
[1060](#1060)
[1061](#1061)    pub require_literal_separator: bool,
[1065](#1065)
[1066](#1066)    pub require_literal_leading_dot: bool,
[1072](#1072)}

[1096](#1096)            require_literal_separator: false,
[1097](#1097)            require_literal_leading_dot: false,
[1098](#1098)        }
[1099](#1099)    }

[1360](#1360)    #[test]
[1361](#1361)    fn test_pattern_matches_case_insensitive_range() {
[1362](#1362)        let pat_within = Pattern::new("[a]").unwrap();
[1363](#1363)        let pat_except = Pattern::new("[!a]").unwrap();
[1364](#1364)
[1365](#1365)        let options_case_insensitive = MatchOptions {
[1366](#1366)            case_sensitive: false,
[1367](#1367)            require_literal_separator: false,
[1368](#1368)            require_literal_leading_dot: false,
[1369](#1369)        };
[1370](#1370)        let options_case_sensitive = MatchOptions {
[1371](#1371)            case_sensitive: true,
[1372](#1372)            require_literal_separator: false,
[1373](#1373)            require_literal_leading_dot: false,
[1374](#1374)        };
[1375](#1375)
[1376](#1376)        assert!(pat_within.matches_with("a", options_case_insensitive));

# GlobError in glob - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/glob/0.3.3/glob/struct.GlobError.html

`pub struct GlobError { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A glob iteration error.

This is typically returned when a particular path cannot be read to determine if its contents match the glob pattern. This is possible if the program lacks the appropriate permissions, for example.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# MatchOptions in glob - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/glob/0.3.3/glob/struct.MatchOptions.html

```
pub struct MatchOptions {
    pub case_sensitive:
```
[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub require_literal_separator: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub require_literal_leading_dot: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
}## Expand description

Configuration options to modify the behaviour of `Pattern::matches_with(..)`.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.case_sensitive)

`case_sensitive: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Whether or not patterns should be matched in a case-sensitive manner. This currently only considers upper/lower case relationships between ASCII characters, but in future this might be extended to work with Unicode.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.require_literal_separator)

`require_literal_separator: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Whether or not path-component separator characters (e.g. `/` on
Posix) must be matched by a literal `/`, rather than by `*` or `?` or
`[...]`.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.require_literal_leading_dot)

`require_literal_leading_dot: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Whether or not paths that contain components that start with a `.`
will require that `.` appears literally in the pattern; `*`, `?`, `**`,
or `[...]` will not match. This is useful because such files are
conventionally considered hidden on Unix systems and it might be
desirable to skip them when listing files.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/glob/lib.rs.html#1074-1100)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-MatchOptions)### impl [MatchOptions](https://docs.rs/struct.MatchOptions.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/glob/lib.rs.html#1074-1100)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-MatchOptions)

### impl [MatchOptions](https://docs.rs/struct.MatchOptions.html)

Constructs a new `MatchOptions` with default field values. This is used
when calling functions that do not take an explicit `MatchOptions`
parameter.

This function always returns this value:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
MatchOptions {
    case_sensitive: true,
    require_literal_separator: false,
    require_literal_leading_dot: false
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

The behavior of this method doesn’t match `default()`’s. This returns
`case_sensitive` as `true` while `default()` does it as `false`.

# Paths in glob - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/glob/0.3.3/glob/struct.Paths.html

`pub struct Paths { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An iterator that yields `Path`s from the filesystem that match a particular
pattern.

Note that it yields `GlobResult` in order to report any `IoErrors` that may
arise during iteration. If a directory matches but is unreadable,
thereby preventing its contents from being checked for matches, a
`GlobError` is returned to express this.

See the `glob` function for more details.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

[elements of this](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.PartialOrd.html)

`PartialOrd`[with those of another. The comparison works like short-circuit evaluation, returning a result without comparing the remaining elements. As soon as an order can be determined, the evaluation stops and a result is returned.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html)

# Pattern in glob - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/glob/0.3.3/glob/struct.Pattern.html

`pub struct Pattern { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A compiled Unix shell style pattern.

-
`?`matches any single character.
-
`*`matches any (possibly empty) sequence of characters.
-
`**`matches the current directory and arbitrary subdirectories. To match files in arbitrary subdirectories, use`**/*`.This sequence **must**form a single path component, so both`**a`and`b**`are invalid and will result in an error. A sequence of more than two consecutive`*`characters is also invalid.
-
`[...]`matches any character inside the brackets. Character sequences can also specify ranges of characters, as ordered by Unicode, so e.g.`[0-9]`specifies any character between 0 and 9 inclusive. An unclosed bracket is invalid.
-
`[!...]`is the negation of`[...]`, i.e. it matches any characters**not**in the brackets.
-
The metacharacters `?`,`*`,`[`,`]`can be matched by using brackets (e.g.`[?]`). When a`]`occurs immediately following`[`or`[!`then it is interpreted as being part of, rather then ending, the character set, so`]`and NOT`]`can be matched by`[]]`and`[!]]`respectively. The`-`character can be specified inside a character sequence pattern by placing it at the start or the end, e.g.`[abc-]`.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/glob/lib.rs.html#608-730)#### pub fn [new](https://docs.rs#method.new)(pattern: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [PatternError](https://docs.rs/struct.PatternError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/glob/lib.rs.html#608-730)

#### pub fn [new](https://docs.rs#method.new)(pattern: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [PatternError](https://docs.rs/struct.PatternError.html)>

This function compiles Unix shell style patterns.

An invalid glob pattern will yield a `PatternError`.

Escape metacharacters within the given string by surrounding them in
brackets. The resulting string will, when compiled into a `Pattern`,
match the input string and nothing else.

Return if the given `str` matches this `Pattern` using the default
match options (i.e. `MatchOptions::new()`).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use glob::Pattern;
assert!(Pattern::new("c?t").unwrap().matches("cat"));
assert!(Pattern::new("k[!e]tteh").unwrap().matches("kitteh"));
assert!(Pattern::new("d*g").unwrap().matches("doog"));
```
